questions.q: Per this lesson, what does an Apex 'best practice' actually represent?
options: An arbitrary stylistic preference with no functional consequence
A convention that exists specifically because it avoids a known, reproducible failure mode
A rule enforced by the Apex compiler itself
A requirement imposed only on managed packages
questions.explain: Every best practice covered in this course maps to a specific, observed way Apex code breaks — bulkification prevents limit breaches, recursion guards prevent infinite trigger loops, and so on.

questions.q: Why is hardcoding a RecordType Id as a literal string dangerous?
options: RecordType Ids are case-sensitive and always cause a compile error
Record Ids are not guaranteed to be the same across sandboxes, scratch orgs, and production, so code can silently misbehave when deployed to a different environment
Apex doesn't allow Id literals at all
RecordType Ids expire after 90 days
questions.explain: A RecordType Id that is correct in one org's sandbox is very likely different in production, and a hardcoded literal doesn't adjust — it just silently points at the wrong (or nonexistent) record in the new environment.

questions.q: What is the recommended way to reference a specific RecordType at runtime instead of hardcoding its Id?
options: Query it by DeveloperName, which stays stable across environments, e.g. via getRecordTypeInfosByDeveloperName()
Always use the first RecordType returned by a generic query with no filter
Store the Id in a custom label and never update it
RecordTypes cannot be looked up at runtime; the Id must be hardcoded
questions.explain: Looking up a RecordType by its DeveloperName (which is stable across sandboxes, scratch orgs, and production) avoids the environment-specific-Id problem entirely.

questions.q: What does 'design pattern' mean in the practical Apex community sense this lesson describes?
options: A Salesforce-mandated structure that every Apex class must follow
A reusable, named solution to a recurring code-organization problem, often originating from community conventions or open-source frameworks
A specific Lightning Web Component template
A feature exclusive to Enterprise Edition orgs
questions.explain: Design patterns like trigger handlers or Selector/Service layering are community-converged conventions for organizing code, not a structure Salesforce itself enforces on every org.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly called out in this lesson as a sign a catch block may be hiding real problems?
options: Catching a specific exception type like DmlException
Logging the exception message before rethrowing it
An empty catch (Exception e) {} block that silently swallows every exception
Using try/catch at all
questions.explain: An empty catch block that swallows every exception without handling or logging it hides real problems instead of deliberately handling exceptions where recovery is meaningful.
